thread:
Mira: Heads up — after the kernel bump on a subset of us-west-2 GPU hosts we're seeing intermittent NCCL hangs during multi-node allreduce. Happens ~1-2x/hr, affects 8-node jobs only. :rotating_light:
Devon: Any packet logs or dmesg snippets? sounds like RoCE path trouble.
Mira: Posting the short logs I grabbed from one implicated host and a node peer. Not much in dmesg besides QP RST spam.
Mira: ```
May 03 12:03:02 host-123 kernel: mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: NIC QP 0x3a2 RST, state=ERR
May 03 12:03:02 host-123 kernel: ib_core: detected qp fatal error on port 1
May 03 12:03:02 host-123 nccl: NCCL INFO AllReduce -> hang at op ctx 0x7f9
```
Sam: QP RST usually means peer sent a REJ or underlying transport reset. Could be asymmetric routing/MTU mismatch. Did you run ibv_devinfo / ib_stat?
Mira: Ran quick check, here's ibv_devinfo -v on both nodes:```
hca_id: mlx5_0
        transport:                      InfiniBand (0)
        fw_ver:                         16.27.1040
        phys_port_cnt:                   2
        port:   1
                state:                  PORT_ACTIVE
                max_mtu:                4096
                active_mtu:             2048
                gid_tbl_len:            128
```
Ingrid: active_mtu 2048 vs 4096 max — could be PMTU along the path forcing 2k. If one switch path uses VXLAN/overlay it might fragment. Any vxlan/vtep changes in the fabric?
Devon: Also check switch PFC and ECN config — if DCB/PFC is partially enabled you can get deadlocks with RoCEv2.
Mira: I pulled tcpdump on UDP port used by RoCEv2 and saw packet sizes around 3500 sometimes, and I saw ICMP frag-needed from a mid-hop. So PMTU indeed bouncing.
Mira: ```
12:03:01.123456 IP host-123 > peer-234: UDP, length 3500
12:03:01.123457 IP peer-234 > host-123: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1500
```
Sam: That explains QP resets — the driver tears down QPs when congestion/fragmentation causes repeated failures. Two immediate mitigations: 1) lower MTU on the HCA to 1500 (or 2048 consistent across path), 2) avoid overlay on east-west (disable VXLAN/GENEVE for RDMA subnet).
Ingrid: Can we pin RDMA traffic to the internal non-overlay vlan? There was a recent CNI tweak that added cross-host tunneling for pod traffic.
Devon: Check CNI annotations and the routing table. If some traffic uses underlay and some overlay, you get asymmetric routes which break RoCEv2 (it relies on consistent 5-tuple).
Mira: Quick experiment: I set vf mtu to 1500 on mlx5 on one host and re-ran a small allreduce. No hangs for 20min.
Mira: Command used: `ip link set dev eth1 mtu 1500` and `echo 1500 > /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/1/pkey_vec` (note: pkey change was exploratory).
Sam: Good repro. Next steps: schedule cluster-wide policy to align HCA MTU with fabric PMTU, and push a fix to CNI to avoid overlay for RDMA subnet. Also file a vendor ticket for kernel bump interaction with mlx5 that may have changed fragmentation behavior.
Devon: I'll open a runbook entry: check ICMP frag-needed on RDMA paths, check active_mtu, and verify that switch fabric supports jumbo frames or has path MTU consistent. Also add a temporary alert for QP RST spikes.
Mira: Created a short alert in @netbot: `RDMA_QP_RST > 10 / 5m` to catch regressions.
netbot: alert created (RDMA_QP_RST, severity=high)
Ingrid: FYI ops — if we can't keep MTU consistent quickly, we should fallback those jobs to intra-node only (single-host NCCL) via scheduler node-affinity while we remediate. Saves costs and avoids failed experiments.
Mira: Agree — I'll add a scheduler constraint for the affected nodepools and roll a config change to reduce host HCA MTU to 1500 as a conservative stopgap.
Sam: Long term: we need eBPF-based path-checks in CI to validate RDMA paths on upgrades. For now, good triage. :thumbsup:
